title: Isolation Refusals, a Patient Escape and Threats to Burn a Treatment Center Expose Response Bottlenecks
detail: A response-monitoring report published 7 September 2026 catalogued a string of community-resistance incidents between 30 August and 4 September that are slowing the DRC's Ebola response even as contact-tracing coverage sits just above threshold nationally (86%, versus 89.8% in Ituri but only 83.3% in North Kivu, 73.9% in Tshopo, 72.1% in Haut-Uélé and 69.7% in Bas-Uélé). In Ituri, health teams logged 17 to 21 isolation refusals per day across the reporting window, and unclaimed bodies awaiting Ebola testing peaked at 42 in a single day before declining to 7-11 in subsequent days; in Haut-Uélé's Pawa health area, a body was forcibly removed from a treatment center and released at a checkpoint without testing, and 10 of 24 mapped health areas were flagged as active resistance zones. In North Kivu's Katwa health zone, a confirmed patient escaped from isolation and local residents threatened to burn down a new treatment center under construction; a separate confirmed patient in Lubero refused transfer to a transit center. In Tshopo, community opposition blocked epidemiologists from closing a contact-tracing ring around the province's 20th case. Separately, teachers in Mambasa's Ituri school zone 3 asked authorities to suspend classes or shift to remote learning given the epidemic's progression in nearby Niania health zone, roughly 350km from Bunia.
